sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Shekhar Kumar Yadav,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned AGA for the State and perused the material on record.
Learned counsel for the informant is also present.

2. The applicants seek bail in Case Crime No. 465 of 2023, under Sections 147, 306, 506 IPC and Section 3/5 (1) of UP prohibition of Unlawful conversion of Religion Act, P.S. Bidhuna, District Auraiya, during pendency of trial.

entities.text: Unlawful conversion of Religion Act, P.S. Bidhuna
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. In short, the prosecution story is that son of informant, namely, Rohit Kumar was having friendship with son of Sattar Khan.
The deceased was also having good relation with the daughter of Sattar Khan.
The informant's son also kept talking to daughter of Sattar Khan.

Sattar Khan and other co-accused persons including applicant wants to solemnize marriage of informant's son with Tulli Khan And Another vs State Of U.P. on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47615032/

sentences.text: the daughter of co-accused Sattar Kan, if the son of the informant convert his religion but the same was refused by son of informant.

It is further alleged that on 15.11.2022 at about 07.00 o'clock the applicant along with other co-accused persons armed with Lathi, Danda, Knife, Gadasa with the intention to kill, threatened the son of informant to convert his religion failing which they will be ruined.

It is further alleged that upon intervention of the villagers, informant son's life was saved and while leaving the place, the accused persons again threatened to kill the entire family members of informant and her son if he will not convert his religion, due to this reason, the son of informant has committed suicide on 18.11.2023.
4. The contention as raised at the Bar by learned counsel for the applicants is that applicants are quite innocent and have been falsely implicated in the present case.
The applicants have never committed any offence as alleged in the impugned FIR.
The investigating officer has recovered the mobile phone of the deceased, thereafter, on that basis, the applicants have been implicated in the present case.

Further contention is that earlier a FIR was lodged by co-accused Salman Khan against the deceased and his family members under Sections 363 and 366 IPC in which during investigation Section 376 IPC as well as 3/4 POCSO Act was added.
Due to this reason, the impugned FIR has been lodged against the applicants and other co-accused persons as a counterblast to the FIR lodged by the applicants against the son of informant.
Further contention is that applicants have never given any threat to the deceased to change his religion even the applicant has never visited the house of the deceased.
Nothing incriminating article has been recovered from the possession or pointing out the applicant.

There is no independent eye witness of the alleged incident and even if the allegation made in the FIR are taken at their face value in entirety, no offene under Section 306 IPC is made out against the applicants.

It is argued that the applicant is languishing in jail since 28.11.2023.
5.

Lastly, it is submitted that bail application of co accused namely Banti Khan @ Nafees Khan whose bail application was heard and rejected by this Court vide order dated 13.02.2024 passed in Criminal Misc Bail Application No. 1493 of 2024

entities.text: Criminal Misc Bail Application No. 1493 of 2024
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
has been granted interim bail by the Hon'ble Apex Court passed in SLP (Cri) No. 12158 of 2024 on 20.09.2024 on the ground of detention and further co accused Salman Khan has also been granted interim bail by the Hon'ble Apex Court in SLP (Crl)
No. 14996 o 2024 dated 08.11.2024 respectively.
6. Per contra, learned AGA as well as learned counsel for the informant have vehemently opposed the prayer for grant of bail to the applicants but does not dispute the aforesaid facts.

7. Upon hearing learned counsel for the parties, perusal of record and considering the complicity of accused, severity of punishment as well as totality of facts and circumstances, at this stage without commenting on the merits of the case, I find it a fit case for bail.
However, any observation made herein-above, will not affect the trial of the case.

8. Let the applicants- Tulli Khan and Tunnak Khan, who are involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on each of them furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.

sentences.text: (i) The applicants shall file an undertaking to the effect that they shall not seek any adjournment on the date fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in Court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.

(ii) The applicants shall remain present before the Trial Court on each date fixed,
either personally or through their counsel.
In case of their absence, without sufficient cause, the Trial Court may proceed against them under Section 229-A IPC.

(iii) In case, the applicants misuse the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure their presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C., may be issued and if applicants fail to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation

,
then, the Trial Court shall initiate proceedings against them, in accordance with law,
under Section 174-A IPC.
(iv) The applicants shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicants is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.

(v) The Trial Court may make all possible efforts/endeavour and try to conclude the trial within a period of one year after the release of the applicants.
9.
In case of breach of of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

10. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
